problem.title: Pivot Student Certification Exam Scores
problem.prompt: You are analyzing a course platform's certification exam data. The `exam_attempts` table stores every exam attempt in long format: each row is one student's score on one exam subject. Your task is to pivot this data into a wide-format report showing each student's highest score per subject as separate columns. Specifically, produce one row per student with columns `student_id`, `sql_score`, `python_score`, and `data_viz_score`, where each score column holds the MAX score that student achieved on that subject's exam (students may attempt the same exam multiple times). If a student has never attempted a particular subject's exam, that column should contain NULL. Include the `students` table to display `student_name` alongside `student_id`. Order the final result by `student_id` ascending. Output columns (in order): `student_id`, `student_name`, `sql_score`, `python_score`, `data_viz_score`.
problem.schema_ddl: CREATE TABLE students (student_id INT PRIMARY KEY, student_name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL); CREATE TABLE exam_attempts (attempt_id INT PRIMARY KEY, student_id INT NOT NULL, subject VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL, score INT NOT NULL, attempt_date DATE NOT NULL);
problem.example_input_data: INSERT INTO students (student_id, student_name) VALUES (101, 'Alice Chen'), (102, 'Bob Kumar'), (103, 'Carol Martinez'), (104, 'David Lee'); INSERT INTO exam_attempts (attempt_id, student_id, subject, score, attempt_date) VALUES (1, 101, 'SQL', 85, '2024-01-15'), (2, 101, 'SQL', 92, '2024-02-10'), (3, 101, 'Python', 78, '2024-01-20'), (4, 102, 'SQL', 88, '2024-01-18'), (5, 102, 'Data Viz', 91, '2024-02-05'), (6, 103, 'Python', 95, '2024-01-25'), (7, 103, 'Data Viz', 89, '2024-02-01'), (8, 104, 'SQL', 76, '2024-01-22');

composite_moves: reshape (pivot subject into sql_score, python_score, data_viz_score using MAX CASE)

hints: You need to transform category values ('SQL', 'Python', 'Data Viz') into separate columns in a single row per student.
Use a GROUP BY on student_id with MAX(CASE WHEN subject = 'SQL' THEN score END) AS sql_score, and similar expressions for the other two subjects.

Join the students table to get student_name, then group by student_id and student_name. Each CASE expression will pick the matching subject's score, and MAX will select the highest across multiple attempts.
problem.answer_key: SELECT s.student_id, s.student_name, MAX(CASE WHEN e.subject = 'SQL' THEN e.score END) AS sql_score, MAX(CASE WHEN e.subject = 'Python' THEN e.score END) AS python_score, MAX(CASE WHEN e.subject = 'Data Viz' THEN e.score END) AS data_viz_score FROM students s LEFT JOIN exam_attempts e ON s.student_id = e.student_id GROUP BY s.student_id, s.student_name ORDER BY s.student_id;

_meta.scenario: an online course platform tracking course completion and certification

user_solution:
/*
1. join
2. pivot
*/
SELECT
    s.student_id,
    s.student_name,
    MAX(CASE WHEN e.subject = 'SQL' THEN e.score END) AS sql_score,
    MAX(CASE WHEN e.subject = 'Python' THEN e.score END) AS python_score,
    MAX(CASE WHEN e.subject = 'Data Viz' THEN e.score END) AS data_viz_score
FROM students AS s
LEFT JOIN exam_attempts AS e
ON s.student_id = e.student_id
GROUP BY s.student_id, s.student_name
ORDER BY s.student_id;
